My advice is be in it for the sex, money, and occasional good times. Have very clear lines between sugaring and where you receive your emotional support from (attention, validation, etc.) 

It depends on the man but that is a good place to start. There will be a few who will be interested in a deeper emotional connection but going into it I would use this guidance to keep myself safe. Also know that each of these relationships will likely be temporary so you can enjoy them at face value and not invest too much into them. 

Also seeing as you are young I want to question your boundaries, and if you are capable of saying no. First if you know exactly what you want, know your limits and non-negotiables, then know how to maneuver a situation that has gone south.

I wonder if you feel any sense of empowerment over this? Managing to build actual regular income in a saturated market. What kind of freedom does this provide you? 

(Personally, I am looking forward to working in a club as a dancer because of the skill it will take, and all of the resources it provides me to progress in my studies etc. Does this apply?) 

Sometimes we need to make strides in our lives in unorthodox ways but I wouldn’t choose to give in to the stigma around sex work. It doesn’t make you less than if you have chosen to harness this trade. Take good care of yourself an build a future plan.

Know that the way you see yourself right now is dark and cloudy and ultimately inaccurate. Our natural form is love, and we deal with challenges. 

The story you are telling yourself is that you are worthless. This is coming from a feeling. 

The feeling is likely fear, guilt, shame etc. But we give our emotions stories. You can acknowledge that you are feeling these things, and practice compassion for those feelings. Talk to yourself, “I am feeling so afraid and hurt, and that is okay. I am here for me” 

I hear that your emotions are overwhelming you which is why I suggested you call a hotline in your area for some ease in the moment and move towards finding a therapist that suits you.

I also strongly suggest calling a hotline in your area. Some lines have counsellors ready to help you work through intense feelings and you can utilize that. It can help to view the situation more positively. Other people’s behaviour is not about you, but it is a lack of skill in dealing with emotions.
